about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

references: Smart, D. F. and Shea, M. A. 2005, A review of geomagnetic cutoff rigidities for earth-orbiting spacecraft, Adv. Space Res. 36, 2012: Størmer's cut-off; for vertical arrival R_c = (μ₀ M c / 16π r²) cos⁴λ, about 14.9 GV at Earth's equator. doi:10.1016/j.asr.2004.09.015
atoms.shown: R_c = (μ₀ M c / 16π r²) cos⁴λ  (vertical arrival)

equation.name: How hard a cosmic ray must hit to get through the field
equation.formula:
m0 = max(M, 0)
cl = abs(cos(lat))
Rc = if m0 <= 0 or r <= 0 then 0 else mu0 * m0 * c / (16 * pi * r * r) * (cl * cl * cl * cl)

M.name: strength of the world's magnet (dipole moment)

Rc.name: least rigidity a cosmic ray needs to get in

source.text: Smart, D. F. and Shea, M. A. 2005, Adv. Space Res. 36, 2012

explain.curious: A magnetic field turns cosmic rays aside, most strongly at its equator. Near the magnetic poles the field lines point straight down and let them in, which is why aurorae and the highest radiation doses are found there.
explain.science: Størmer's result for a dipole: a particle needs at least the cut-off rigidity (momentum per charge) to arrive vertically at magnetic latitude λ and distance r. It falls as 1/r², so a field shields less with height.

params.description: rigidity, GV, below which the star's wind has already thinned the cosmic rays
integral spectral index of cosmic rays at high rigidity

references: Navas, S. et al. (Particle Data Group) 2024, Review of Particle Physics: Cosmic rays, Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001: primary nucleon intensity falls as about E^−2.7 above a few GeV (integral index about 1.7). doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001

equation.name: Share of cosmic rays strong enough to get in

R0.name: where the star's wind thins the cosmic rays, GV

s.name: share of the cosmic-ray dose above the cut-off

source.text: Navas, S. et al. (Particle Data Group) 2024, Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001

explain.curious: Cosmic rays come in all energies, many more weak ones than strong. A field that turns away the weak ones removes most of the dose in space.
explain.science: The integral cosmic-ray spectrum above rigidity R falls as a power of R with index about 1.7; the star's wind already removes most particles below a few GV, so the share bends over below R₀.

references: Clem, J. M. and Dorman, L. I. 2000, Neutron monitor response functions, Space Sci. Rev. 93, 335: ground count rate against cut-off follows N(R_c) = N₀ (1 − exp(−α R_c^−k)); attenuation in air about 140 g/cm² (barometric coefficient about 0.7 % per hPa). doi:10.1023/A:1026508915269
atoms.shown: share = 1 − exp(−α R_c^−k),  R_c in GV

equation.name: Share of the ground's cosmic-ray rate left under the field
equation.formula:
gv = Rc * per_GV
s = if gv <= floor then 1 else 1 - exp(-alpha * gv ^ (-k))

floor.name: cut-off below which there is none, GV

s.name: share of the polar ground rate left

source.text: Clem, J. M. and Dorman, L. I. 2000, Space Sci. Rev. 93, 335

explain.curious: Under a thick air, only the strongest cosmic rays make showers that reach the ground, and the field cannot turn those aside. So the field changes the ground dose by about half, not a hundredfold.
explain.science: Neutron monitors show how a ground rate falls with cut-off: the Dorman function, fitted at sea level, integrates the shower yield over the cosmic-ray spectrum.

references: Atri, D., Hariharan, B. and Grießmeier, J.-M. 2013, Galactic cosmic ray-induced radiation dose on terrestrial exoplanets, Astrobiology 13, 910: the air column, not the field, is the main shield for a world with thick air. doi:10.1089/ast.2013.1052

Zeitlin, C. et al. 2013, Measurements of energetic particle radiation in transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory, Science 340, 1080: 1.84 mSv per day in interplanetary space near 1 AU. doi:10.1126/science.1235989

UNSCEAR 2008, Sources and effects of ionizing radiation, Annex B: cosmic rays at sea level give about 0.39 mSv a year (0.28 directly ionising, mostly muons, and 0.11 from neutrons). https://www.unscear.org/unscear/en/publications/2008_1.html
atoms.shown: D = D₀ s [(1 − f_μ) w (w S_space + (1 − w) S_ground) + f_μ e^(−X/λ_μ) S_ground],  w = e^(−X/λ_n)

equation.name: Radiation dose under a world's air
equation.formula:
x = max(X, 0)
w = exp(-x / Ln)
share = w * ss + (1 - w) * sg
D = max(D0, 0) * sky * ((1 - fm) * w * share + fm * exp(-x / Lm) * sg)

X.name: air above, mass per square metre

ss.name: share above the cut-off in space

sky.name: share of the sky not hidden by the world

source.text: Atri, D., Hariharan, B. and Grießmeier, J.-M. 2013, Astrobiology 13, 910

explain.curious: Air is a shield. Earth's column of air weighs as much as ten metres of water, and cuts the cosmic-ray dose about a thousandfold; Mars's thin air barely helps.
explain.science: Two-part attenuation: the nucleonic cascade falls off with about 140 g/cm²; muons, made in it, penetrate much further and dominate at sea level. The body itself blocks the sky below the horizon.
